  WHERE feature_id IS NOT NULL AND feature_id != ''

Bug IDs correctly land here via `reindexCommitTrailers` (`reindex_trailers.go:37-48`) which uses `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO git_commits ... feature_id=<parsed-id>`. The trailer parser (`reindex_trailers.go:98`, `parenWorkItemRe`) matches `bug-` IDs and `parseTrailers` is confirmed correct by `reindex_trailers_test.go:21-27`.

- `cmd/wipnote/arch_cmds.go:415-450` — `resolveWorkItemPaths` calls `dbpkg.ListFilesByFeature(database, workItemID)`, which queries `feature_files WHERE feature_id = ?`. This is structurally fine for bug IDs.

**Why worktree paths, home-dir paths, and tmp transcripts appear:**

The slices' own `complete --learning` ran while the active feature was one of the slice implementation features. `ingest.go` recorded every Read/Edit/Write call's raw `file_path` into `feature_files`. During those sessions the agent read `.claude/worktrees/<name>/...` paths (worktree-absolute), `~/.claude/agent-memory/...` paths (home-dir memory files), and `/tmp/.../task-output-*.md` transcript paths. ### Data Observations

No direct SELECT was possible on a DB with ingest-sourced `feature_files` rows (the active DB has 0 rows). The bug description is authoritative: cards `learning-feat-359312ab` and `learning-feat-5a312c8f` contain paths of the form `.claude/worktrees/<name>/...`, `~/.claude/agent-memory/...`, and `/tmp/.../...`.

### Durable Fix Design

**Three-layer fix: normalize at ingest, normalize at capture, validate in store.**

**Layer 1 — Fix ingest.go (prevents future garbage)**

`cmd/wipnote/ingest.go:277`, after `fp := extractIngestFilePath(tc.InputJSON)`, add:

```go
fp = paths.MustNormalize(fp, projectDir)
if strings.HasPrefix(fp, "unresolved:") || fp == "" {
    continue  // skip outside-repo paths
}
```

`projectDir` is already available in the ingest call chain (passed through from the reindex session context). If it is not directly available at the callsite, it can be threaded from `runIngest` or resolved from `wipnoteDir` via `filepath.Dir(wipnoteDir)`.

Outside-repo paths that get `unresolved:` prefix are actively harmful in `feature_files` (they will never match arch card globs and inflate the card's paths list). Skipping them is correct. If future callers genuinely need outside-repo awareness, a separate table is the right place.

**Layer 2 — Normalize at capture time in createLearningCard (defense in depth)**

`cmd/wipnote/arch_cmds.go:519-530`, before `card := &corearch.Card{...}`:

```go
repoRoot := filepath.Dir(wipnoteDir)
cleanPaths := make([]string, 0, len(paths))
for _, p := range paths {
    p = paths.MustNormalize(p, repoRoot)
    if strings.HasPrefix(p, "unresolved:") || p == "" {
        continue
    }
    cleanPaths = append(cleanPaths, p)
}
// deduplicate
card := &corearch.Card{Paths: deduplicateStrings(cleanPaths), ...}
```

This ensures that even if `feature_files` somehow contains stale garbage (pre-fix rows, or rows from a session that ran before the ingest fix), the learning card still receives only repo-relative paths.

**Layer 3 — Validator rule in arch validate (not verified — inferred from Card struct)**

`core/arch/card.go` — `Card.Paths []string` has no validation today beyond being parsed from YAML. The `arch validate` command exists (`archValidateCmd`, `arch_cmds.go:31`). The durable rule to add to `Validate(card)`:

```
For each path in card.Paths:
  - reject if filepath.IsAbs(path)            → "path must be repo-relative, got absolute: <p>"
  - reject if strings.HasPrefix(path, "unresolved:") → "path is unresolved host-local path: <p>"
  - reject if strings.HasPrefix(path, "../")  → "path escapes repo root: <p>"
  - warn (not error) if path starts with ".claude/agent-memory" or contains "/tmp/" 
    → these are almost always mistaken captures
```

The rule is **warn-on-suspicious, error-on-absolute** so it does not break bootstrap cards that deliberately reference `docs/` or `internal/` subdirectories. There is no legitimate case for an absolute path in `card.Paths` (globs are matched against repo-relative paths in `MatchCards`).

**Does this break arch bootstrap or agent-context skill injection?** No. Bootstrap cards are created with explicit `--paths` flags from `arch_bootstrap.go` — those paths come from the manifest/plan, not from `feature_files`, so they are already repo-relative strings. Skill-context injection calls `runArchResolve` which reads `card.Paths` as glob patterns matched against repo-relative input paths — relative patterns work correctly, absolute ones silently never match (which is the current broken state). Adding the validator surfaces the bug rather than creating a new one.

**Migration/repair for the two existing garbage cards:**

Cards `learning-feat-359312ab` and `learning-feat-5a312c8f` live in `.wipnote/arch/`. They need surgical `arch edit` calls:

```bash
wipnote arch edit learning-feat-359312ab --paths "cmd/wipnote/,core/arch/"
wipnote arch edit learning-feat-5a312c8f --paths "cmd/wipnote/,core/arch/"
```

The correct paths can be derived from `git diff-tree` on the commits linked in each card's `links:` frontmatter field. The fix PR should include these edits committed alongside the code change, or a one-time repair script that reads each garbage card, extracts `links`, runs `git diff-tree` on each linked commit, normalizes, and rewrites `paths:`. The latter is better because it is repeatable for any future garbage cards discovered later.

**Alternatives rejected:**

- "Filter at ListFilesByFeature" — moves the fix too late; the garbage is already in `feature_files` and would persist until a reindex. The correct barrier is at write time.
- "Store only reindex-sourced paths in feature_files (disable ingest path)" — loses real-time file attribution that live session hooks and the overlap-detection system depend on.
- "Validator as error on all absolute paths including `unresolved:`" — would break any card manually created before this fix that happens to have a legitimate-looking path that got the unresolved prefix. Warn-on-suspicious + error-on-raw-absolute is the safe policy.
